notes: Anau culture of southern Turkmenistan; infobox 'c. 4500 BC - 1100 BC', 'Geographical range: Southern Turkmenistan'. The page gives two starts: 'around 4500 BC in the Neolithic period' (Anau IA) and 'around 4000 BC' in its introduction; 4500 follows the infobox and the Jeitun page. Anau IB 'reached an extent of 10-15 hectares' and parallels Namazga I (c. 4000-3500 BC on the Namazga-Depe page); no dates for Anau II and III. The dossier runs far beyond the 3400 BCE horizon because the infobox does and nothing else draws the Kopet Dag until the Achaemenids; its shape is the Turkmen side of the Jeitun country (confidence 2: the page says only 'centred in southern Turkmenistan'). The page says 'The Namazga culture was contemporary to the Anau culture' (Namazga-Depe 'covering some 60 hectares' in Namazga V; no dossier for the Namazga or the later Altyn-Depe, abandoned 'Around 1600 BC'), so the cell-level shape of the late centuries is a single stand-in. Anau pottery 'found as far as Shir Ashian Tepe in Iran's Semnan Province' is trade/influence and not drawn. No successor on the page. No area figure.
